findings.body:
**Write and check the exact UTF-8 vector bytes.**

On Windows, CPython translates LF to CRLF when `print` writes to stdout and when `Path.write_text()` writes the fixture. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/3.14/Python/pylifecycle.c)) The stdout comparison in `apps/crq-python/test_ledger_vector_emit_b1.py` Line 35 then fails. `--check` can miss a CRLF fixture because `read_text()` normalizes line endings. Write UTF-8 bytes to stdout and the fixture, and compare fixture bytes in `--check`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed change</summary>

```diff
-        print(text, end="")
+        sys.stdout.buffer.write(text.encode("utf-8"))
...
-        existing = FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if FIXTURE.exists() else ""
-        if existing != text:
+        existing = FIXTURE.read_bytes() if FIXTURE.exists() else b""
+        if existing != text.encode("utf-8"):
...
-        FIXTURE.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+        FIXTURE.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
```
</details>






Also applies to: 689-689
findings.title: Write and check the exact UTF-8 vector bytes.

findings.body:
**Bind the drain-refusal queue digests to the baseline snapshot.**

The fixture at `apps/crq-python/test_vm_unit_switch.py:177-178` sets `baseline_sha256` and `restored_sha256` to `"0" * 64`. The same fixture's snapshot state records `queue.json` as `"c" * 64`. `STATE` is defined at line 41 and reaches the snapshot through `observation()` at line 141 and the prepared baseline at line 75. The checker never compares these two views. `_drain_refusal_ok` checks the queue digests only against each other, and `_snapshot_preserved` compares only the before and after snapshots with each other. The fixture can therefore pass while the queue evidence contradicts itself.

The guest source shows the intended relation. It sets `baseline_sha256` to the digest of the saved queue bytes, and it requires the restored state to equal the saved state. The baseline digest should match the baseline state's `queue.json` digest.

Make the fixture consistent with `STATE`:

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fixture fix</summary>

```diff
         "queue": {"before_sha256": "1" * 64, "after_sha256": "1" * 64,
-                  "baseline_sha256": "0" * 64, "restored_sha256": "0" * 64},
+                  "baseline_sha256": "c" * 64, "restored_sha256": "c" * 64},
```

</details>

Also bind `baseline_sha256` to the baseline snapshot's `queue.json` digest in the drain-refusal check. Add a negative test with a mismatched value, so the checker rejects it.
findings.title: Bind the drain-refusal queue digests to the baseline snapshot.

findings.body:
**Give each scope its own copy in `_review`.**

`_review` assigns one `rows` list to `requested_scope`, `input_scope`, and `reviewed_scope`. `_regenerated` copies the record with `copy.deepcopy`, which keeps the three references pointing to one shared copy. The mutations at lines 466 and 468 therefore change all three scopes together. `scope_digest` still reflects the original rows, so the requested-scope digest check at `review_ledger.py:203` rejects both cases before the exceedance check at line 206 runs. Neither vector reaches the condition it names.

Copy each scope separately so each mutation changes only its own scope. Then regenerate `fixtures/crq-ledger-b1/vectors.json` with `python3 ledger_vector_emit_b1.py --write`, because the expected outcomes for these two cases change.

<details>
<summary>Proposed change</summary>

```diff
-        "requested_scope": rows,
-        "input_scope": rows,
-        "reviewed_scope": rows,
+        "requested_scope": copy.deepcopy(rows),
+        "input_scope": copy.deepcopy(rows),
+        "reviewed_scope": copy.deepcopy(rows),
```
</details>
findings.title: Give each scope its own copy in `review`.
